text:
carmen: quick flag  new auto-pin policy attempted to revert a tenant to v1 overnight and the owner complained. we need an owner-consent flow for account-level auto-pins.
dean: saw the email thread. owner says automated change broke an internal pipeline. we should not auto-pin account-wide without an explicit opt-in.
irene: proposal: auto-pin can run only for routes unless the account owner has opted into 'account-level auto-reverts'. default behavior: auto-pin route-level only and notify owners with one-click accept/decline.
ops-bot: auto: incident note appended: auto_pin_attempt(account=velox, scope=account, projected_savings=$120/day, triggered_by=telemetry-agent)
pat: consent flow sketch: when auto-pin candidate detected -> create a modal/email with summary (projected_savings, affected_routes_count, risk_score) -> owner can click Accept (apply ephemeral account-pin TTL=12h) or Decline (suppress further auto-pins for 24h). record decision in audit log.
ux-lee: UX notes: include a single-line summary in console banner with buttons Accept / Decline and a link to a small details pane. show confidence band for projected savings and an option "only apply to tagged routes (batch|offline)".
carmen: telemetry: we must tag auto-pin events with owner_decision and time_to_ack so we can measure friction. Also emit pre/post token metrics and pin_provenance=auto|manual.
dean: add a safety: if owner does not respond within 2h, auto-pin should not escalate to account scope. route-level auto-pin can still apply after owner-notify but account-level requires explicit accept.
irene: API example for owner acceptance webhook:
```bash
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/auto_pin/decision \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"account":"velox","decision":"accept","scope":"account","ttl":"12h","reason":"owner-ack-2024-11-05"}'
```
pat: runbook update: 1) detect candidate; 2) send owner notify with accept/decline; 3) if accept -> apply pin + emit telemetry; 4) if decline -> suppress for 24h and file observation; 5) for emergency ops (pin:emergency) allow manual account pin bypassing consent but require audit reason.
ux-lee: visual: modal must show a predicted hourly cost delta and a small graph of historical token rate, plus a link "preview route-level impact" that runs a dry-run for 15m.
ops-bot: auto: follow-up reminder scheduled in 30m.
carmen: action owners: irene->policy guard rails + webhook API; ux-lee->modal copy & mock; dean->notification templates + legal consult; pat->runbook + telemetry tags. I'll draft a quick comms note to owners explaining the new consent flow.
pat: will also add an alert that fires if an accepted account-pin reduces cost < 15% after 30m so we can review and revert if needed.
dean: good. small dev note: runtime must surface connection_drain_seconds in the modal so owners understand change won't be immediate.
irene: acknowledged. will include drain estimate and the dry-run link in the webhook payload.
carmen: thanks all, aim to land consent flow MVP behind a feature flag this week.
